code: # known: group a has 11 rows, 2 with the outcome, 8 without, 1 missing. # Group b has 11 rows, 6 with the outcome, 4 without, 1 missing. # Odds ratio of b against a: (6 / 4) / (2 / 8) = 6. # null: the outcome does not depend on the group. data_raw <- function(scenario, sim) {   switch(scenario,     real = data.table::fread(file.path(org::project$data_raw, "d.csv")),     known = data.table::data.table(       `Person ID` = 1:22,       Group = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 11),       X = rep(c(31, 45, 38, 52, 40, 33, 47, 36, 50, 42, 44), 2),       Outcome = c(rep(c(1, 0, NA), c(2, 8, 1)), rep(c(1, 0, NA), c(6, 4, 1)))     ),     data.table::data.table(       `Person ID` = 1:400,       Group = sample(c("a", "b"), 400, replace = TRUE),       X = replace(round(stats::rnorm(400, 50, 10)), sample(400, 20), NA),       Outcome = stats::rbinom(400, 1, 0.3)     )   ) } data_clean <- function(d) {   data.table::setnames(d, janitor::make_clean_names(names(d)))   d[, outcome := as.integer(outcome)]   d } data_cohort <- function(d) {   cp <- cohort::CohortPipeline$new(d)   cp$exclude_and_track("root", "missing outcome", "is.na(outcome)")   cp }

code: make_table1 <- function(data, argset) {   pbn::table1(data$d, by = "group", vars = CFG$vars) }  # A negative control: with a permuted group, the true odds ratio is 1. fit_permuted <- function(data, argset) {   d <- data.table::copy(data$d)   d[, group := sample(group)]   fit <- stats::glm(outcome ~ group, family = "binomial", data = d)   data.frame(term = "or_group_b", estimate = exp(stats::coef(fit)[["groupb"]])) } fit_models <- function(data, argset) {   if (plnr::is_run_directly()) {     argset <- p$get_argset("null__sim_0003__models__2")     data <- p$get_data("null__sim_0003__models__2")   }   rhs <- if (argset$adjust == "none") "group" else "group + x"   fit <- stats::glm(stats::as.formula(paste("outcome ~", rhs)), family = "binomial", data = data$d)   data.frame(term = "or_group_b", estimate = exp(stats::coef(fit)[["groupb"]])) }

MUST return data.frame least one row columns assertion, expected, observed pass. expect_real() optional. scenario known tests two outputs numbers person computed hand. test analysis behaves data large untidy real data. scenario null tests mean log odds ratio 3 simulations within 0.5 zero groups differ. test analysis finds difference . 400 rows, one log odds ratio standard error 0.22, mean 3 0.13.
code: expect_known <- function(results) {   t1 <- results$table1   m <- results$models   observed <- c(     t1$events[t1$var == "outcome" & t1$grp == "b"],     m$estimate[m$adjust == "none"]   )   expected <- c(6, 6)   data.frame(     assertion = c("outcome events in group b", "crude odds ratio of b against a"),     expected = expected,     observed = observed,     pass = abs(observed - expected) < 1e-6   ) }  # results holds the 3 simulations stacked, and each data.frame has a first # column sim. expect_null <- function(results) {   m <- results$models   p <- results$permuted   log_or <- mean(log(m$estimate[m$adjust == "none"]))   log_or_permuted <- mean(log(p$estimate))   data.frame(     assertion = c("simulations", "mean crude log odds ratio", "mean permuted log odds ratio"),     expected = c("3", "-0.5 to 0.5", "-0.5 to 0.5"),     observed = c(length(unique(m$sim)), round(log_or, 3), round(log_or_permuted, 3)),     pass = c(length(unique(m$sim)) == 3, abs(log_or) < 0.5, abs(log_or_permuted) < 0.5)   ) }
